# Animesh Singh

<div class="home-role">PhD Student in Computer Science and Engineering</div>
<div class="home-institution">Indian Institute of Technology Hyderabad</div>

I study the **behavior and correctness of network programs**, with a focus on **eBPF bytecode analysis** and **network function verification**.

My goal is to develop practical tools that help explain what deployed programs do and identify correctness issues when multiple network functions interact.

::: {.home-section .home-about}
<div class="home-section__eyebrow">ABOUT ME</div>

## Making network programs easier to understand and verify

I am a PhD student in the Department of Computer Science and Engineering at **IIT Hyderabad**. My research lies at the intersection of **networked systems**, **program analysis**, and **software correctness**.

I work on analyzing compiled eBPF programs without requiring source code. I am also investigating how to reason about the behavior of network functions when they are composed into a chain.
:::

::: {.home-research-card}
<div class="home-card__number">01 / BYTECODE</div>

### eBPF bytecode analysis

Analyzing compiled eBPF programs to understand packet accesses, helper calls, memory effects, and program behavior.
:::

::: {.home-research-card}
<div class="home-card__number">02 / CORRECTNESS</div>

### Network function verification

Checking properties of individual network functions and identifying correctness issues that arise from their composition.
:::

::: {.home-research-card}
<div class="home-card__number">03 / SYSTEMS</div>

### Networked systems

Building practical program-analysis methods for programmable network dataplanes and deployed network functions.
:::
